label: late copy-phase steps of short sequences (L=3 final output; L=4 last two outputs on o/j/t/i/m/3/r/h inputs)
explanation: Fires only during the copy phase (never in the original phase or on <DEL>), and only from recall_idx>=2, concentrated near the end of the copy (to_go=0 holds 72% of mass, to_go=1 17%). It is strongest on short sequences: the final copy step of L=3 sequences fires 87% of the time and carries the top activations (e.g. u o h <DEL> u [o]), holding ~38% of mass. In L=4 sequences it fires on the last two copy steps, mostly when the fed-back input is o, j, t, i, m, 3, r or h; o is the strongest input token overall (8x lift). For L>=5 there is a diffuse low-magnitude tail at mid/late copy steps with the same input-token preference that the predicate does not capture. Magnitude is highest for L=3 final step with input o/t/3/m/j. Does not fire on first occurrences of a token, in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on the first two copy steps.
